newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai silk industry in crisis, factories close.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai silk industry in crisis, factories close.

text.p: An inability to keep pace with changing market demand and a flood of high-quality imports have shut down more than half of Shanghai's 40 silk factories, the Liberation Daily reported on Sunday.
In the first nine months of 1996, China's output of silk products was 26.17 million metres, down 45.8 percent from the same 1995 period, it said.

In all 1995, total sales volume of silk in China was nearly five billion metres, of which 2.9 billion was produced domestically and the rest imported, with output in Shanghai alone rising 44 percent over the 1994 level, it said. In the first 10 months of 1996, sales of silk products in Shanghai fell 3.2 percent from the same 1995 period after falling 28 percent in all 1995 from all 1994, with consumers becoming more choosy in their purchases, it said.

With supply greatly exceeding demand, inventory levels have soared in Shanghai, forcing mergers, closures and shut-downs of the city's silk factories, leaving less than 20 in operation, down from more than 40 previously, it said. The key problem is the gap in technology between Chinese products and imports, with Chinese factories unable to match the quality standards of the imported products, it said but gave no more details.
